To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
3D CNNs can be used to accurately predict the presence of Alzheimer’s disease, based on MRI scans of the brain.

(i) 3D convolution networks outperform other classifiers on the ADNI data and produce state-of-the-art results; (ii) the best performance is achieved by using a combination of 3D convolution and sparse autoencoder; (iii) 3D CNNs can be trained to classify Alzheimer’s disease with high accuracy, and (iv) 3D convnets can be trained to predict the disease status with high accuracy.
3D CNNs can achieve state-of-art results in the classification of Alzheimer’s disease, and that the best performance is obtained using the full 3D volume, without any spatial preprocessing.
